summary: Standards (atip.midway.09): the audit proves that every exit-1 code has a line, that each kept code is registered and that some source spells it (a text search of the sources), and that the moved one is gone; it cannot prove the judgments in the lines (hand-written classes), and 'built by a source' is satisfied by any occurrence of the name, a comment included. So a code that is kept for the wrong reason, or a kept code whose only remaining occurrence is a doc comment, passes. The negative paths the brief names are there (a code the table lacks, a kept code no source builds, a moved code that returns each fail the check). Mitigated by atip.midway.03-08, which run the real init path. Blast radius: the audit protects against a forgotten exit-1 code, not against a wrong classification.
